description: Bird Safe Saskatoon highlighted City Hall's bird collision problem.
Public art could provide bird-safe window solutions.
Over 500 residents support bird-safe City Hall windows.

chips.text: Is the city allowed to use City Hall windows as a public art space?
Over 500 residents signed a petition supporting bird deterrents at City Hall.
City Hall's north facade is one of Saskatoon's worst sites for bird collisions.

segments.title: Bird Collision Problem and Art Solutions
segments.takeaway: Mercy Harris presented the severe issue of bird collisions at City Hall windows, proposing art-based deterrents as an effective and aesthetic solution.

segments.title: Saskatoon Nature Society's Support for Bird-Safe City Hall
segments.takeaway: David Forbes reinforced the urgency of making City Hall's north facade bird-safe and advocated for public art as a creative and necessary solution.

segments.title: Committee Discussion on Project Funding and Implementation
segments.takeaway: The committee engaged in a detailed discussion regarding the project's estimated costs, potential funding avenues, and the process for integrating public art into the bird deterrent initiative.

description: Public Art Advisory Committee reports 2025 accomplishments to Council.
Report demonstrates committee's relevance and current activities.

chips.text: Some members admitted they had not read the annual report before the meeting.
Committee members questioned how to track work and reports for future reference.
